topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
source_evidence: ETF investors may pay their brokers sales commissions with each purchase or sale of ETF shares. A brokerage commission is often structured as a flat fee charged every time an investor trades. With a flat fee, the smaller the amount traded, the larger the percentage cost per trade is.
answer: ETF brokerage commissions are charges a broker may collect when you buy or sell ETF shares. They are often a flat fee for each trade. When a flat fee applies, it takes up a larger percentage of a smaller trade than of a larger trade. These commissions are not shown in the ETF’s prospectus fee table, so check with your broker about any charges that apply.
